steps.content: Fortunately, the girl doesn't end up dying or getting swallowed by quicksand.
She's let many down, but as long as that one person recognizes her, everything's worth it.

steps.speaker: Eirene
steps.content: Chief, it's your turn.
E-M-P! Mess! Can you hear me?
And you're still absorbed in the ending of the young girl's story.
Excuse me... But that story was too...

steps.speaker: Eirene
steps.content: It's not a story, it's a trial given to me by my father.
I know, but still... it sounds a bit unimaginable.

steps.speaker: Eirene
steps.content: I remember I've told you, he's able to sit on his throne now because he's trampled over his own family many times.

steps.speaker: Eirene
steps.content: If I died, it would only prove that I wasn't qualified to stand next to him.

steps.speaker: Eirene
steps.content: But fortunately, not only did I survive... but my ability also awakened.
That was when you became a Sinner!

steps.speaker: Eirene
steps.content: Yes... I've heard of two ways parents react to their child turning into a Sinner.

steps.speaker: Eirene
steps.content: They either become even more protective and refuse to let the government take their kid, reluctant to lose them.

steps.speaker: Eirene
steps.content: Or they throw the kid out like a piece of dirty rag, afraid of having the slightest connection with a Sinner.

options: Then... which reaction did you get?

choices.text: Then... which reaction did you get?

steps.content: Eirene shrugs, skillfully placing a chess piece where one of yours stands, devouring it. You recognize the piece, it's the queen.

steps.speaker: Eirene
steps.content: I guessed right. The one who bought the desert bandits to ambush me on the route was indeed my father.

steps.speaker: Eirene
steps.content: His intention was clear. If I died, he'd pretend he'd never had this daughter, and if I lived... it'd prove that I was still useful.

steps.speaker: Eirene
steps.content: That's why when I lived... when I became a Sinner, he was gratified.

steps.speaker: Eirene
steps.content: He told me to feel proud of myself... because he was going to send me to the DisCity to lay the foundation for his great plan.

steps.speaker: Eirene
steps.content: That was the second time he said that. The first time he told me to feel proud of myself was the only time I defeated him at chess.
As you're talking, Eirene has once again besieged your pieces. There's nothing worth analyzing on the chessboard, Eirene has simply been devouring all your pieces ruthlessly.
In other words, you've established Quinn at your father's will?
You move your piece one step to the side. You've decided to struggle a bit more and open up the spot so that you may bring the king out.

steps.speaker: Eirene
steps.content: Correct. He'd planned the entire roadmap for me. As long as I followed his instructions, nothing could go wrong. Then again, what he'd planned was not easy to achieve either.

steps.speaker: Eirene
steps.content: But I'm a Campbell, after all. Perhaps I was born with... a rebellious instinct in me.

steps.speaker: Eirene
steps.content: I thought I could undermine him slowly. I didn't expect to... fail completely.
Eirene lowers her gaze and stares at the chessboard, her thoughts undecipherable.
That's also why I hope you can come with me to Fraser City.
As the chief, I can't let a Sinner fall under someone else's control. As your acquaintance... I think you're too competent to be controlled by him.
Also, I'd like to clarify that the shackles... are in fact not a form of control...
Tak! You hear the crisp sound of a piece falling, and the corner of Eirene's mouth is slightly lifted, interrupting your sentence.

steps.speaker: Eirene
steps.content: Checkmate.
What?

steps.speaker: Eirene
steps.content: I'm sorry, you lost, Chief.
On the chessboard, the king you've racked your brains to move out has been blocked by Eirene's queen. You're stuck.

steps.speaker: Eirene
steps.content: This is speed chess. As a beginner, you did pretty well playing against me.

steps.speaker: Eirene
steps.content: But still... Thank you, Chief. My mind feels a lot clearer now.
You stare at the chessboard occupied by black pieces and feel perplexed. Is she genuinely confused?
In that case... what's your answer?

steps.speaker: Eirene
steps.content: I'll come with you... Indeed, I should break free from the control.
Eirene picks up the permit on the desk and smiles at you.

steps.speaker: Eirene
steps.content: Whenever you're ready.
There are no windows in the sand cruiser's cockpit. You can only observe what's going on outside through the navigation panel.
Sailing off that towering wall, the surrounding structures are beginning to dwindle in both height and number. The sand is stirred up by both the wind and the oars, slowly covering the sky.

steps.speaker: Eirene
steps.content: No. It's just that I've realized that this sand cruiser... looks like the one owned by my family at that time.

It's indeed a copy manufactured based on the Campbell family's ship. The trade terms with Fraser City contain a blueprint of the sand cruiser. And if I remember correctly, Quinn also owns a sand cruiser manufacturer, doesn't it?
Miss Eirene, I thought you must know? This sounds more bizarre than me thinking you may have motion sickness.

steps.speaker: Eirene
steps.content: Excuse me. This ship is a pretty old model. I thought you would use a newer sand cruiser produced by Quinn, it'll be much faster.
...This is just to pay Fraser City some respect.

steps.speaker: Eirene
steps.content: We're still about thirty minutes away from the unruled areas of WhiteSands. Would you like to play some more chess with me, Chief?
Within thirty minutes, can I reach a level where I may be able to last a few turns with Mr. Campbell?

steps.speaker: Eirene
steps.content: You're certainly an idealist.
That's enough time for you to defeat me five or six times, Miss Eirene.

steps.speaker: Eirene
steps.content: Wouldn't it be fun?
Eirene shrugs and looks at you with amusement.
She's literally just told you that horrifying story not long ago, yet there's no trace of fear on her face, even though she's going to see her own family who once tried to murder her.

steps.speaker: Eirene
steps.content: Perhaps that's the secret behind the Campbells' successes.
Eirene seems to have read your mind.

steps.speaker: Eirene
steps.content: The business world is a battlefield. Affection plays no role here.
After that, the conversation ceases between you and Eirene.
On the navigation panel, the color outside the window has turned into an endless stretch of white with no other colors. You realize you've probably crossed into the unruled areas.
You're going to face that businessman deemed cruel and ruthless by many... Bryce Campbell.

steps.speaker: Vibrating noises
steps.content: Boom...
What's that?

steps.speaker: Eirene
steps.content: It's from a sand cruiser... Are there others following you?
No, our main purpose this time is not a violent confrontation.

steps.speaker: Navigator
steps.content: Chief, several old sand cruisers have just appeared out of nowhere on our route!

steps.speaker: Navigator
steps.content: Moreover... They're approaching us, looking ready to fight! We're already within their shooting range!

steps.speaker: Eirene
steps.content: They're Campbell's freighters, Chief.

steps.speaker: Eirene
steps.content: Although these are old models, with their number and the weapons equipped on them, they can deal a fatal blow to us.
As they're speaking, some obscure shouts from the outside are reaching the cockpit.
Those people are chanting Bryce's name and asking the MBCC's chief to get lost or kiss Bryce's feet.
This operation has been disguised as a regular trade visit. We've been betrayed.
As you're still frowning and considering what to do, dense gunfire is already blasting around you. The next round of bombardment may hit the cabin.
Eirene...
You raise your head to look straight at her.
Feeling your gaze, she laughs softly.

steps.speaker: Eirene
steps.content: If you trust me... let me sail it.
I also hope you can trust my decision.
Eirene bypasses you and walks straight to the navigator's seat to begin operating the panel. Her movements are smooth and without any hesitation.
The freighters on the other side are still attacking, but under Eirene's navigation, your ship begins dodging and retreating.

steps.speaker: Navigator
steps.content: Is... is this route safe? We haven't tested if there's quicksand...

steps.speaker: Eirene
steps.content: A Campbell can escape WhiteSands with their eyes closed.

steps.speaker: Eirene
steps.content: Have you never heard of this saying?
Without stopping her hands, Eirene winks at the navigator.

steps.speaker: Navigator
steps.content: Excuse me...

steps.speaker: Eirene
steps.content: ...Hmm, you're very young, after all.
Under Eirene's navigation, your sand cruiser begins sailing in another direction. Although the Campbell freighters are chasing after you closely, you haven't been hit so far.
Eirene navigates so skillfully that it's as if this ship were the one that had been through fire and water with her back in the day.
Thanks for navigating the ship, hang in there. Other armed crew members, please follow me to the deck...
Those guys have been quiet for a while. Who knows what they're up to next.

You lead a group to the deck to check the stern of the ship. You've guessed right. While you weren't aware, they tied a rope to the stern of the ship and are now jumping onto your freighter one by one.
Stop them. We can't let them get inside the cockpit!
You command the team to disperse and strike back at the intruders.

steps.speaker: Eirene
steps.content: Watch out, the freighter at ten o'clock is shooting at you guys! Hold on tight!
Eirene's voice comes from the PA system on the ship. You throw yourself to one side and lie down behind a container.
Boom!!
As a deafening explosion sounds, the entire ship shakes violently for a while as if it's grabbed by a giant invisible hand.
When the smoke clears up, you finally realize your ship has been hit.

steps.speaker: Eirene
steps.content: Ugh... Apologies, Chief. I couldn't dodge that one hit.
Eirene's voice sounds a little feeble as well, perhaps because she bumped into something with the shock just now.

steps.speaker: Eirene
steps.content: It must have been a seasoned gunner. They changed the trajectory at the moment it was fired... That was insane...
But before you can recover from the shock, a second shell has already been fired.

steps.speaker: Eirene
steps.content: Chief! Take cover!!
The static noise in Eirene's voice is gone. The ship has stopped and she's come out of the cockpit.
With a severe look on her face, she raises her hand toward the incoming shell.

steps.speaker: Eirene
steps.content: I won't let you have your way again.
The shell explodes in mid-air. Debris and sparks bloom in the air, falling down on the deck, making cracking noises.
It's Eirene's special ability.

steps.speaker: Eirene
steps.content: Chief, you can order me.

steps.speaker: Eirene
steps.content: Otherwise, both you and I may not make it back alive.
What do you mean?!
Eirene gives a wry smile and points at the ship facing you.

steps.speaker: Eirene
steps.content: He... came himself. The one firing the shells is him.

steps.speaker: Eirene
steps.content: Everything I know, I've learned from him. I can never win against him.

steps.speaker: Eirene
steps.content: Unless... you agree to let me use my ability.

As you're talking, more shells keep flying toward you. All of them are blocked by Eirene in mid-air, but it's not difficult to tell that your opponent is set on wrecking this ship, even though some of his own people are on board.

steps.speaker: Eirene
steps.content: Chief, that's our only way out.
You clench your fists and dig your fingernails into your palms, but your hands have long been numbed by firing the gun, so you don't feel any pain at all.
You know you're facing a cutthroat situation, but you don't want to let Eirene use her power. Despite everything, the person on the other ship is her father, and she... has at least once revered him.

options: Allow Eirene to use her power
Not allow Eirene to use her power

choices.text: Allow Eirene to use her power
Not allow Eirene to use her power

steps.content: But I won't allow you to attack him with your special ability. Just block all his shells.
You can't use your special ability on humans.

steps.speaker: Eirene
steps.content: What...?
I mean you can only use your special ability to stop the shells. Leave the rest to me.
You turn around and gather the remaining crew members to escort you back to the cockpit.
The climate in WhiteSands is special. Is there a storm coming soon?

steps.speaker: Navigator
steps.content: Yes, in about three minutes.
Good. I'll ask Eirene to reserve a time interval in three minutes. You guys seize this chance to aim at the opponents and...
Get rid of as many of them as possible.

steps.speaker: Navigator
steps.content: ....Copy that.
You grab a sniper rifle from the weapon rack and gesture for the other crew members to follow you.
The sky is getting dark, but you're not sure whether it's due to the smoke from the gunfire or the gathering clouds.
The wind is becoming stronger. The dark smoke resulting from the shells exploding in mid-air by Eirene's power is diffusing in the air bit by bit.
You squat and lean against the lookout, the rifle in place. The soldiers behind you are ready and waiting for your command.
Everything you see now is through the small window of the rifle scope.
You're waiting, waiting for that person to appear before the storm...
Everyone, aim at two o'clock...
A blur of black barges into your sight from the edge of the window.
The figure leans half of his body forward, as if wanting to operate the artillery.
You know this is the best and the last chance you'll get.
Ceaseless gunshots are echoing in the comms, and you see the target falling down slowly amid the converged gunfire.
The shells closing in on the ship have dyed the sky red. But as if blocked by something, they stop flying and instead are struggling, contorting, and exploding in the sky.
Eirene's power is indeed terrifying.
...Did we succeed?

The wind is still blowing, clearing up the obstacles blocking your sight. Fortunately, the opponents have stopped attacking. A smear of red is dripping down the enemy's artillery. Finally, you let out a sigh of relief.
Your hands are still shaking. After you get down from the lookout, you remove the magazine and pass the rifle to the soldiers while mocking yourself for trembling so badly.
You give a slightly resigned smile and walk to Eirene.
Eirene is standing at the bow of the ship, but her eyes keep avoiding the ship carrying her father.
I'm sorry. The most I could do was not let you be the one to do it.

steps.speaker: Eirene
steps.content: ...I understand what you mean.

steps.speaker: Eirene
steps.content: I just can't believe that he... really died, just like that.

steps.speaker: Eirene
steps.content: Perhaps... he was really getting old.
On the gap blasted open by the shells at the stern, a piece of hard steel has been sliced off, dangling and moaning like a frail old man.
Unstable to withstand the wind, it finally falls with a thud.

steps.speaker: Eirene
steps.content: Let's go, Chief. Let's go and witness the beginning of a new era for the Campbells.
Sure, but first we should do a quick cleanup to preserve all the evidence. I suppose the Campbells are all difficult to deal with, just like him.

steps.speaker: Eirene
steps.content: In that case, I'll let you know...
Eirene walks back, and turns back to wink at you when she reaches the other end. The previous sadness in her seems to have all vanished.

steps.speaker: Eirene
steps.content: There are at least ten other tricky Campbell children like me in Fraser City.
Your father... was a virile man.
